introduction: This level covers the fundamental principles of static charges, the forces between them, and the electric fields and potentials they generate. This forms the bedrock for all of electromagnetism.

core_concepts.title: Quantization of Charge
core_concepts.description: The total charge on any body is always an integral multiple of the elementary charge of an electron ($e$): $Q = \pm ne$, where $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.

core_concepts.title: Coulomb's Law
core_concepts.description: The electrostatic force between two point charges: $F = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}$. It is mathematically similar to Newton's law of gravitation, but this force can be both attractive and repulsive.

core_concepts.title: Electric Field ($E$)
core_concepts.description: The region around a charge where other charges experience an electrostatic force. $E = F/q$. Due to a point charge: $E = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \frac{q}{r^2}$.

core_concepts.title: Electric Potential ($V$)
core_concepts.description: The work done in bringing a unit positive charge from infinity to a specific point against the electrostatic force. $V = W/q$. Due to a point charge: $V = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \frac{q}{r}$.

important_entities.name: Permittivity of Free Space ($\epsilon_0$)
important_entities.significance: A measure of how easily electric field lines can permeate through a vacuum. The constant $\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$ has a value of $9 \times 10^9$.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Electric Field ($E$) and Force ($F$) are vector quantities; when calculating their magnitudes, DO NOT put the signs ($+, -$) of the charges into the formula. Determine direction visually. Potential ($V$) and Potential Energy ($U$) are scalar quantities; you MUST include the charge signs in their formulas.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: E is the negative gradient of V
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Electric field is equal to the negative derivative of potential with respect to distance: $E = -\frac{dV}{dr}$. Electric potential strictly decreases in the direction of the electric field.

exam_strategy_tips: The work done in moving a charge along an Equipotential Surface is always strictly zero ($W=0$), because the potential difference ($\Delta V$) between any two points on it is zero.
